title: Glenny's rule: ask someone who knows
summary: Glenny said to ask questions of someone able to answer; Guesnon names good and weak players.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: If I remember rightly now, it's coming to me a little bit. It seems like you said once, Glennie said, if you're going to ask somebody, don't ask a damn fool the question. Oh, yeah.

Oh, yeah. Always. No, that's what he said. He said, every man can be taught something by somebody. But just so the man is not a damn fool. That's all. He said, make sure when you go to a man to ask him concerning something that the man is able to tell you what to do. And he's right. You understand? That's right. In other words, if I wanted to know something on the banjo, I'd ask people like Kimball and Sales. You understand what I mean? I wouldn't ask Black Walter because he wouldn't know. He's my friend and all, but he just don't know. You know what I mean? He's just sitting up there playing all night. But ask him, make G7. He don't know what G7 is at all. He just played by what he hear in his ear. But you could ask people like Sales and Kimball, anything, and they was able to ask it musically. You know, they were good musicians.
